newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends at 8-yr low against U.S. dlr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends at 8-yr low against U.S. dlr.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed at an eight-year low against its U.S. counterpart on Monday while reflecting quarter-end demand for the greenback, but dealers said they saw limited downside room ahead.
The local unit finished at T$27.908 against Saturday's T$27.888 close, marking its lowest level since a T$28.03 finish on January 7, 1989.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$293 million.
Dealers noted strong seasonal demand for the U.S. dollar, especially from importers.
"Importers were buying U.S. dollars to make overseas payments," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
She said she also saw greenback buying from commercial banks.
But other dealers said the local dollar likely would stabilise at the current level due to the central bank's unwillingness to let it drop further.
"The central bank does not necessarily mind a weak local currency to boost exports, but it certainly does not want to see the rate plunge too far too soon," said another dealer.
A T$27.88-92 range was seen for Tuesday.
